Core elements: Template — streamlined main deck (top metrics + one‑line variances) with full appendix for pre‑read; Meeting flow — 45‑minute core + optional 15‑minute finance deep‑dive for flagged appendix items; Decisions & Actions — mandatory table mirrored to a shared tracker (Short title; Owner person + team; Due date; Context/rationale + link; Stakeholders only for cross‑team items); Feedback — 4‑question 1–5 post‑meeting form and a two‑cycle debrief.

Thanks — here are five short Q&A pairs you can drop under the snapshot.  

Q: Why are we doing this? A: We’re piloting a simpler meeting and tracker to reduce meeting time and stop follow‑ups—especially cross‑team items—from falling through.  

Q: What’s actually changing? A: A streamlined main deck (top metrics + one‑line variances) with an appendix pre‑read, a mandatory "Decisions & Actions" row that mirrors to a shared tracker, and a 45‑minute core meeting with an optional 15‑minute finance deep‑dive for flagged appendix items.  

Q: What’s expected on owners and due dates? A: Every action must have one named owner (person + team) and a due date before the meeting closes; cross‑team items must list involved teams and a coordinating owner; our goal is ≥90% documented ownership as a shared improvement target, not a punitive metric.  

Q: How much extra work is this (really)? A: We kept fields short (title, owner, due date, one‑line context, stakeholders only for cross‑team), owners update status in the tracker within 48 hours, and the post‑meeting feedback is four quick 1–5 ratings plus an optional one‑line comment (~30 seconds).  

Q: What if the pilot doesn’t hit the targets? A: After two cycles we’ll review results and iterate (examples: relax timing, require appendix pre‑reads, or scope a small tooling follow‑up); this is a learning pilot and we’ll adjust together.
